title: Self-Evolving Recommender Systems: A Survey of Agent-Driven Model Improvement and How to Evaluate It

meta.claim: Auditing code/config-level self-evolving recommenders on eight evaluation criteria shows the field cannot yet separate real gains from selection noise, sampled-metric artefacts or weak baselines; a shared sealed, full-ranking, budget-accounted protocol is missing.

01-idea.summary: Survey; primary claim = taxonomy (what evolves x selection signal) + 8-criterion evaluation audit

02-related-work.summary: 154 refs; 6 clusters (search-space AutoML, generic program evolution, code/config-level self-evolving recsys, generative-component evolution, policy/memory self-improvement, evaluation methodology); no prior survey of cluster C

03-benchmarks.summary: Evaluation settings in use, metric pathologies, blind spots, requirements for a shared evolver benchmark

04-methodology.summary: Two-axis taxonomy: evolved object L0-L4+meta x selection signal S1-S6; loop anatomy; comparison table

05-challenges.summary: 11 limitations from full-text audit of 17 systems; L1 selection-on-noise + L2 no null control ranked first; Roelofs counter-evidence recorded

06-alignment.summary: keep, sharpened; no subsumption (4 nearest surveys read in full)

07-refine.summary: Draft paper.tex (10 pp acmart): taxonomy, systems, audit of 22+5 systems generated from audit.csv, reporting standard, recforge, open problems, threats
